title: Ezekiel 31
paragraphs: ¹ In the eleventh year, in the third month on the first day, the word of the LORD came to me: ² "Son of man, say to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his hordes: Who can be compared with you in your greatness? ³ Consider Assyria, once a cedar of Lebanon, with beautiful branches overshadowing the forest and towering high, its top above the thick branches. ⁴ The waters nourished it, deep springs made it grow tall; their streams flowed all around its base and sent their channels to all the trees of the field. ⁵ So it towered higher than all the trees of the field; its boughs increased and its branches grew long, spreading because of abundant waters.

⁶ All the birds of the air nested in its boughs; under its branches all the animals of the wild gave birth; all the great nations lived in its shade. ⁷ It was majestic in beauty, with its spreading boughs, for its roots reached down to abundant waters. ⁸ The cedars in the garden of God could not rival it, nor could the fir trees equal its boughs, nor could the plane trees compare with its branches — no tree in the garden of God could match its beauty. ⁹ I made it beautiful with abundant branches, the envy of all the trees of Eden in the garden of God. ¹⁰ Therefore this is what the Sovereign LORD says: Because the cedar towered on high and lifted its top above the thick branches, and because it was proud of its height,

¹¹ I gave it into the hands of the ruler of the nations, for him to deal with according to its wickedness. I cast it aside, ¹² and foreigners, the most ruthless of nations, cut it down and left it. Its branches fell on the mountains and in all the valleys; its boughs lay broken in all the ravines of the land. All the nations of the earth came out from under its shade and left it. ¹³ All the birds settled on the fallen tree and all the wild animals lived among its branches. ¹⁴ This happened so that no tree growing by water may ever again tower high, lifting its top above the thick branches. No water-fed tree can ever again reach up and tower above the others. They are all destined for death, for the depths of the earth, among mortals who go down to the pit. ¹⁵ This is what the Sovereign LORD says: On the day it was brought down to the grave I covered the deep springs with mourning for it; I held back its streams, and the great waters were restrained. Because of it I clothed Lebanon with gloom, and all the trees of the field withered away.

¹⁶ I made the nations tremble at the sound of its fall when I brought it down to the realm of the dead, to be with those who go down to the pit. Then all the trees of Eden, the choicest and best of Lebanon, all the trees that had been well watered, were comforted in the earth below. ¹⁷ Those who had lived in its shade, its allies among the nations, had also gone down to the realm of the dead, to those killed by the sword. ¹⁸ Which of the trees of Eden can be compared with you in splendor and majesty? Yet you, too, will be brought down with the trees of Eden to the earth below; you will lie among the uncircumcised, with those killed by the sword. This is Pharaoh and all his hordes, declares the Sovereign LORD.
